title: AI, audits and OSINT featured in House intel bill
summary: The House intel bill would establish an IC chief AI officer, illuminate how agencies fund open-source intelligence, give the IC IG new authorities and more.

title: House Republicans adopt $95 billion package for the Iran war and Trump’s priorities
summary: The House adopted a Republican-only $95 billion budget proposal, a long-shot effort to fund the Iran war and other White House priorities. Speaker Mike Johnson worked Wednesday to push it over objections from Democrats and some GOP holdouts as a priority before the midterm elections. The package includes $73 billion for the Pentagon and other national security needs, $12 billion for farmers struggling under President Donald Trump’s tariffs and $10 billion for voting law changes that are a Trump priority. Democrats argued the money should be spent at home, particularly on efforts to lower costs for Americans. It next goes to the Senate.

title: Space Force doesn’t know how many personnel it needs, watchdog finds
summary: GAO found that the service hasn't established a process to accurately determine its personnel needs and doesn't have a workforce plan to guide future growth.

title: House votes for Department of War renaming as part of an annual defense bill
summary: The House has passed a defense policy bill that incorporates President Donald Trump’s request for a historic $1.15 trillion in spending for the Pentagon. The bill passed Wednesday also would designate the Department of Defense as the Department of War and provide for a pay raise next year of 5% to 7% for service members. The National Defense Authorization Act is generally one of the more bipartisan bills that Congress takes up each year. That’s not the case this year. Democrats took issue with steep spending increases for defense while Republicans attempted to cut numerous non-defense programs. The Senate still has to pass its own version of the bill.

title: He was fired by the White House right after being sworn in. Now a top federal prosecutor is suing
summary: His action creates a first-of-its-kind court case that will test the Justice Department's authority to fire federal prosecutors who are appointed by judges.

title: AI enthusiasm isn’t AI readiness: Why mission clarity must come first

title: FedRAMP and Identity Security: Why federal organizations are consolidating identity security platforms
summary: Identity security consolidation helps federal agencies reduce risk, cut costs and strengthen Zero Trust by unifying governance, access and AI controls.

title: One year later, my layoff from the federal government has become a banishment
summary: Despite our grief and trauma, many of us still want to return to the State Department or another federal agency. But the path back does not exist.

title: Can the right kind of data predict mission success?

title: Government measures compliance, but does accountability help programs succeed?

title: Senate panel advances Jay Clayton’s nomination to lead US intelligence agencies
summary: The Senate Intelligence Committee has advanced the nomination of Jay Clayton, President Donald Trump’s pick to head the nation’s intelligence agencies. The vote was along party lines. The 9-8 vote came after some Democrats had praised Clayton and indicated that they might vote for him. But that shifted after a contentious hearing last week in which Clayton repeatedly refused to say that former President Joe Biden won the 2020 election. Democratic Sen. Mark Warner said during the hearing that he was “bitterly disappointed” in Clayton. The intelligence panel vote sets up a floor vote on Clayton’s nomination, potentially early next week.

title: US civil rights agency moves to end demographic data collection after 60 years
summary: The EEOC has historically used the data to guide its enforcement priorities and inform some of its investigations.

title: Fired DHS, Interior probationary workers challenge MSPB ruling
summary: Ex-probationary staff from DHS and Interior are challenging the MSPB's ruling that it lacks the jurisdiction to determine whether their firings were illegal.
